Song of Songs 1:15: Behold, you are beautiful, my companion! Behold, you are beautiful; your eyes are doves.
Song of Songs 1:16: Behold, you are beautiful, my kinsman, and indeed lovely! Moreover, our bed is shaded.
1 Kings 7:1: King Solomon sent and brought Hiram from Tyre,
1 Kings 7:2: a widow’s son, and he was from the tribe of Naphtali. His father was a Tyrian man, a bronze craftsman, filled with skill, understanding, and knowledge for doing every work in bronze. He was brought to King Solomon and did all the works.
1 Kings 7:3: He cast the two pillars for the house’s porch. The pillar was eighteen cubits high, and a circumference of fourteen cubits encircled it. The pillar’s thickness was four fingerbreadths, with hollow spaces; and the second pillar was the same.
1 Kings 7:4: He made two capitals to place on top of the pillars, of cast bronze. One capital was five cubits high, and the second capital was five cubits high.
1 Kings 7:5: He made two nets to cover the pillars’ capital: one net for one capital and one net for the second capital.
1 Kings 7:6: There was hanging work: two rows of bronze pomegranates interwoven as a net, hanging work, row upon row. He did likewise for the second capital.
1 Kings 7:7: He set up the pillars of the temple’s porch. He set up one pillar and called it Iachoum; he set up the second pillar and called it Boaz.
Song of Songs 5:2: I sleep, but my heart keeps watch. The voice of my kinsman—he knocks upon the door! Open to me, my sister, my companion, my dove, my perfect one, for my head is filled with dew and my curls with the drops of night.
Song of Songs 5:4: My kinsman extended his hand from the opening, and my belly was stirred for him.
Song of Songs 5:5: I rose to open to my kinsman; my hands dripped myrrh, my fingers rich myrrh, upon the handles of the bolt.
Song of Songs 5:6: I opened to my kinsman; my kinsman had gone. My soul went out at his word. I sought him but did not find him; I called him, but he did not answer me.
Luke 11:5: And He said to them, “Which of you will have a friend and go to him at midnight and say to him, ‘Friend, lend me three loaves,
Luke 11:6: since a friend of mine has arrived at my home from a journey, and I have nothing to set before him,’
Luke 11:7: and that man will answer from inside, ‘Do not trouble me. The door is already shut, and my children are in bed with me. I cannot get up and give you anything’?
Luke 11:8: I tell you, even if he will not get up and give to him because he is his friend, yet because of his shameless insistence he will rise and give him as much as he needs.
Song of Songs 7:6: Your head upon you is like Carmel, and the braid of your head is like purple; a king is bound in passageways.
Song of Songs 7:8: This stature of yours has been compared to a palm tree, and your breasts to clusters.
Song of Songs 7:9: I said: I will climb the palm tree; I will grasp its heights. Then your breasts will be like clusters of the vine, and the fragrance of your nose like apples,
Song of Songs 7:10: and your throat like good wine, going straight to my kinsman, suited to my lips and teeth.
Song of Songs 7:11: I am my kinsman’s, and his turning is toward me.
Proverbs 5:15: Drink waters from your vessels and from your spring wells.
Proverbs 5:16: Do not let waters overflow for you from your spring; but let your waters travel into your own squares.
Proverbs 5:17: Let them belong to you alone, and let no outsider share with you.
Proverbs 5:18: Let your fountain of water be your own, and share joy with the wife of your youth.
Proverbs 5:19: Let a deer of affection and a colt of your graces keep company with you. Let your own woman lead you and be with you at every time, for as you move in the company of her affection, you will be one among many.
Proverbs 5:20: Do not be much involved with another woman, nor be held in the arms of one who is not your own.
1 Kings 7:38: Solomon built his own house in thirteen years.
1 Kings 7:39: He built the house with timber from Lebanon’s forest: a hundred cubits long, fifty cubits wide, and thirty cubits high, with three rows of cedar pillars and cedar supports for the pillars.
1 Kings 7:40: He paneled the house above, over the sides of the pillars. The number of the pillars was forty-five, fifteen to a row.
1 Kings 7:41: There were three beams, and space above space in three tiers.
1 Kings 7:42: All the doorways and spaces were square and fitted with beams, with doorway facing door in three tiers.
1 Kings 7:43: The porch of the pillars was fifty cubits long and thirty wide, joined together, with a porch in front of them, and pillars and a thick structure in front of it for the porches.
1 Kings 7:44: There was the porch of the thrones, where he would judge, the porch of the judgment hall.
1 Kings 7:45: He had a house where he would live, with one court opening around these, according to this workmanship; and a house for Pharaoh’s daughter, whom Solomon had married, corresponding to this porch.
Luke 11:1: And it happened that He was praying in a certain place. When He stopped, one of His disciples said to Him, “Lord, teach us to pray, just as John also taught his disciples.”
Luke 11:2: He said to them, “When you pray, say: ‘Father, let Thy name be hallowed. Let Thy kingdom come.
Luke 11:3: Give us day by day our daily bread.
Luke 11:4: And forgive us our sins, for we ourselves also forgive everyone who owes us. And do not bring us into testing.’”
